partners.mechanism_chain: GLUD1 (HGNC:4402) —DISRUPTS→ Glutamate Dehydrogenase Activity (REACT:90127); Glutamate Dehydrogenase Activity (REACT:90127) —DECREASES→ alpha-ketoglutarate (CHEBI:15807); alpha-ketoglutarate (CHEBI:15807) —INCREASES→ Ammonia (CHEBI:17790); Ammonia (CHEBI:17790) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperammonemia (HP:0002131); GLUD1 (HGNC:4402) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperinsulinism (HP:0011362); ALDH18A1 (HGNC:417) —DISRUPTS→ Argininosuccinate Synthetase Activity (REACT:89727); Argininosuccinate Synthetase Activity (REACT:89727) —DECREASES→ Glutamate (CHEBI:17221); Glutamate (CHEBI:17221) —INCREASES→ Ammonia (CHEBI:17790); ALDH18A1 (HGNC:417) —LEADS_TO→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252); ALDH18A1 (HGNC:417) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263); ALDH18A1 (HGNC:417) —LEADS_TO→ Cataracts (HP:0000501). Loss-of-function mutations in GLUD1 disrupt glutamate dehydrogenase activity, leading to accumulation of alpha-ketoglutarate and subsequently ammonia. This hyperammonemia contributes to the phenotype of hyperinsulinism-hyperammonemia syndrome. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in ALDH18A1 impair its role in proline and arginine biosynthesis, impacting argininosuccinate synthetase activity, which in turn affects glutamate levels. Elevated glutamate can contribute to ammonia production. The shared consequence of dysregulated ammonia homeostasis and potentially altered glutamate metabolism links the two disease modules, leading to overlapping phenotypes like developmental delay and hypotonia.
